Parent-of-origin effects and PFAS exposure in human placenta Overview

Parent-of-origin effects and PFAS exposure in human placenta Sean T. Bresnahan Overview This site documents the placenta-poe-pfas pipeline: parent-of-origin effects (POE) on placental gene and isoform expression in GUSTO mother-father-infant trios, and their modification by prenatal PFAS exposure. Chapter Content Workflow stage diagram, inputs, how to run, methods per stage, outputs, caveats Genotyping methods arrays, sample and SNP QC, genotype processing Reports rendered analysis reports Configuration config/paths.sh and config/resources.sh The pipeline runs on an LSF cluster through run_pipeline.sh; every stage is a folder of job scripts and R / Python drivers, with the shared model code in R/. 1 Workflow This document explains how the scripts in this repository fit together, what each stage does, what it needs, what it writes, and how to run the whole analysis from raw genotypes and RNA-seq on an LSF cluster. 1.1 1. Study design in one paragraph GUSTO mother-father-infant trios are genotyped on the Illumina OmniExpressExome-8 v1.2 array. Trios are lifted to GRCh38, assigned to Chinese / Indian / Malay ancestry, phased with the pedigree (SHAPEIT5), and the phased infants are imputed on the SEAD reference panel. The imputed infant variants are projected onto a long-read placenta transcriptome (ESPRESSO + SQANTI3), and each infant’s placental short-read RNA-seq is quantified allele-specifically against a personalised transcriptome (Ornaments). The parents’ genotypes then tell which infant haplotype is maternal and which is paternal, turning haplotype-specific counts into maternal / paternal counts per transcript-SNP and gene-SNP. Negative-binomial mixed models estimate the cohort-level parent-of-origin effect (POE) for each gene and transcript (stage 07) and how that effect changes with maternal or cord-blood PFAS concentrations and gestational diabetes (stage 08). 1.2 2. Before the first run 1.3.1 3.1 Software Tool Used in Configured by LSF (bsub, bjobs) job submission config/resources.sh (queues) bcftools >= 1.16, tabix, bgzip 01-05 BCFTOOLS_ENV (conda env) bcftools build with the +liftover plugin 01_liftover LIFTOVER_BCFTOOLS PLINK 1.9 01 PLINK_MODULE samtools 00 SAMTOOLS_ENV SHAPEIT5 (SHAPEIT5_phase_common) 02_phase SHAPEIT5_VENV Ornaments (ornaments, g2t conversion) 04 ORNAMENTS_VENV Python >= 3.8 with pysam 01 QC, 05 PYTHON_ENV R >= 4.3 (run via Singularity image) 00, 02-04, 06-10 RSTUDIO_SIF, R_LIB_DIR, SING_BIND wget manual SEAD download - R packages: glmmTMB, data.table, dplyr, tidyr, purrr, forcats, stringr, tibble, ggplot2, ggrepel, scales, patchwork, BiocParallel, optparse, readxl, SNPRelate, class, boot, lavaan, dagitty, biomaRt (Bioconductor). 1.3.2 3.2 Configuration All paths and environment names live in config/paths.sh; all LSF resources in config/resources.sh. Every value is a default that can be overridden by exporting the variable before calling run_pipeline.sh. R scripts read the same variables through R/setup.R, so there is one place to edit. Typical first edit: set LAB_DIR, SCRATCH_DIR, the software environment names, and the paths in the GUSTO inputs and references blocks. 1.3.3 3.3 Required inputs Variable Content TRIOS_DIR/<PLINK_PREFIXES>.{bed,bim,fam} PLINK binaries for infants, mothers, fathers (hg19, TOP-strand alleles) HG19_FASTA, HG38_FASTA, HG19_TO_HG38_CHAIN reference genomes (hg19 chr-prefixed) and liftover chain GENETIC_MAP_DIR/chr<N>.b38.gmap.gz GRCh38 genetic maps (SHAPEIT format) INFANT_META_CSV infants with placental RNA-seq: SubjectID, maternal ethnicity FASTQ_DIR/J<fastq id>_{1,2}.fq.gz, FASTQ_ID_MAP paired-end placental RNA-seq; map <SubjectID> <fastq id> TX_FASTA, TX_GTF, TX_CLASSIF long-read placenta transcriptome (ESPRESSO sequences, GTF, SQANTI3 classification) RNASEQ_COVARS_CSV RNA-seq covariates: SubjectID, sex, mother_ethnicity, GA, gdm PFAS_MAT_CSV, PFAS_CHILD_CSV SubjectID + 8 PFAS (PFBA PFOA PFNA PFDA PFUnDA PFBS PFHxS PFOS) with _mat / _child suffixes, first 9 columns PFAS_MAT_COHORT_XLSX, PFAS_CORD_COHORT_XLSX whole-cohort PFAS tables (dose-response annotation only) ARRAY_MANIFEST, DBSNP_*_VCF only for the optional manifest QC EXCLUDE_SAMPLES_FILE optional; one sample ID per line, removed from every model Sample naming: PLINK writes VCF sample IDs as FID_IID. IIDs start with B (infant), M (mother) or P (father); the infant’s FID is the GUSTO SubjectID. Model sample IDs are <SubjectID>_B<SubjectID> with - replaced by _. PFAS scale. PFAS values enter the interaction models exactly as they appear in PFAS_*_CSV (no log transform, no standardisation inside the pipeline). Decide the scale before the first run (for example log2 ng/mL) and write the CSVs accordingly; beta_int is per unit of whatever scale is supplied. 1.4 4. Running the pipeline cd placenta-poe-pfas ./run_pipeline.sh all # dry run: prints the bsub plan, submits nothing ./run_pipeline.sh --submit all # queue every main step with LSF dependencies ./run_pipeline.sh status # receipts done / expected and active jobs per step ./run_pipeline.sh list # the step registry Targets can be a step (02_phase), a stage number (07), all, qc (optional QC steps) or sim (stage 10). Several targets can be combined. Option Effect --submit actually submit (default is a dry run) --force ignore receipts and rerun every selected element --pilot N submit at most N elements of each selected array step --lenient start downstream steps when upstream jobs end (ended()) rather than only after every element succeeded (done()) --tag NAME job-name prefix (default poe) so two copies can run side by side Resume. Each finished job or array element writes RUN_DIR/receipts/<step>.<index>.ok. Steps with all receipts are skipped and array steps resubmit only missing elements, so rerunning the same command resumes after failures. Delete a receipt (or use --force) to redo work. 1.4.1 4.1 The SEAD imputation step (manual) The SEAD server is external, so the pipeline pauses there: ./run_pipeline.sh --submit all runs stages 00-02 and writes the phased infant VCFs to SEAD_UPLOAD_DIR/<group>/<group>_chr<N>.vcf.gz. Steps that need imputed data are not submitted while the SEAD results are missing. Upload each ancestry group to the SEAD server (GRCh38, Rsq >= 0.3 filter). Save the download links of each finished job to config/sead_urls_<group>.txt (gitignored; the links contain access tokens) and run on a login/transfer node: REPO=$PWD bash 03_imputation_SEAD/retrieve_SEAD.sh <group> config/sead_urls_<group>.txt Once every SEAD_DOWNLOAD_DIR/<group>_SEAD/chr<N>.SEAD.GRCh38.dose.vcf.gz exists, run ./run_pipeline.sh --submit all again; finished steps are skipped and the pipeline continues from stage 03. 1.4.2 4.2 Other manual points 00_imprint_db queries Ensembl through biomaRt and needs internet access. If compute nodes are offline, run REPO=$PWD Rscript 00_reference/imprintDB.R on a login node, then touch $RUN_DIR/receipts/00_imprint_db.1.ok. Ornaments is the most expensive step. Run a pilot first (section 8). 1.4.3 4.3 A full run from raw data ./run_pipeline.sh --submit all qc # stages 00-02 (+ manifest QC) # ... SEAD upload, imputation, retrieve_SEAD.sh for each group ... ./run_pipeline.sh --submit 04_ornaments --pilot 2 # optional resource pilot ./run_pipeline.sh --submit all qc # stages 03-09 ./run_pipeline.sh --submit sim # stage 10, independent ./run_pipeline.sh status Logs go to LOG_DIR/<step>.<jobid>.<index>.{out,err}. 1.5 5. Stage-by-stage methods 1.5.1 Stage 00 - references reference_index indexes the hg19 and GRCh38 FASTA files. imprintDB.R maps a curated list of imprinted-gene symbols and aliases to Ensembl gene IDs (IMPRINT_DB) and builds an Ensembl ID to symbol table for every gene in the placenta transcriptome (PLACENTA_DB). 1.5.2 Stage 01 - genotype preparation prep_ped.R / pedigree.lsf: infant-centred trio pedigree from the three .fam files (TRIO_PED: FID IID PID MID SEX PHENO, 0 = parent not genotyped), then make_shapeit5_fam.sh writes the SHAPEIT5 pedigree (offspring father mother, NA for a missing parent) using VCF IDs (FID_IID; set ID_MODE=iid if the VCF uses bare IIDs). plink2vcf.lsf: PLINK 1.9 merge of the three files (SNPs with conflicting alleles across files are dropped), autosomes only, chr-prefixed VCF; bcftools +fixref -m top converts Illumina TOP strand to the hg19 forward strand; bcftools norm --check-ref x drops remaining mismatches. liftover.lsf: drop sites invariant across all trio members, lift hg19 to GRCh38 with bcftools +liftover, sort, split/deduplicate, keep biallelic SNPs whose REF matches GRCh38 (TRIO_VCF_HG38). check_mendel.lsf: PLINK --mendel error rates per trio, individual and SNP (QC report, not a filter). qc/manifest_qc.lsf (optional): aligns the array manifest to hg19 and records which SNPs needed a swap or strand flip. Genotyping and array-level QC are described in reports/genotype_methods.md. 1.5.3 Stage 02 - ancestry and phasing infer_ancestry.R: PCA (SNPRelate) on LD-pruned autosomal SNPs in infants. Infants with reported maternal ethnicity (the RNA-seq subset) train a 3-nearest neighbour classifier on PC1/PC2 that labels the remaining infants; parents inherit their infant’s label. Writes samples_<group>.txt per group. split_by_ancestry.lsf: per group, recompute site statistics and keep biallelic SNPs with missingness <= 0.05, MAF >= 0.05, HWE p >= 1e-6; one BCF per autosome. phase.lsf: SHAPEIT5 phase_common with the trio pedigree and GRCh38 genetic map, per group and chromosome. subset_by_role.lsf: phased infants to bgzipped VCFs for SEAD upload; unphased mothers and fathers kept per chromosome. 1.5.4 Stage 03 - SEAD imputation retrieve_SEAD.sh (manual, see 4.1). filter_sead.lsf: keep biallelic imputed sites with MAF > 0.01 (the server has applied Rsq >= 0.3). merge_sead.lsf: merge the three ancestry groups per chromosome (union of sites; genotypes absent from a group are missing) into IMPUTED_DIR. imputation_qc (optional): site counts before and after filtering, variant density per kb, imputed MAF and R2 distributions. 1.5.5 Stage 04 - allele-specific quantification prep_transcriptome.lsf: list the VCF IDs of infants with RNA-seq (INFANT_SAMPLES) and add 5’->3’ exon_number attributes to the transcriptome GTF (required by Ornaments). g2t_vcf.lsf: project imputed genomic variants onto transcript coordinates (Ornaments), keeping heterozygous sites. g2t_merge.lsf: merge chromosomes for the RNA-seq infants, write a valid header (one contig per transcript), bgzip and index. ornaments.lsf: per infant, extract its phased heterozygous transcriptomic variants, build a personalised transcriptome and index, and run ornaments quant on the paired-end placental RNA-seq. Index files are removed after quantification unless KEEP_TXOME_INDEX=1. txomic_stats (optional): heterozygous variants per transcript. 1.5.6 Stage 05 - parental origin of infant haplotypes assign_POE.py, per chromosome and infant: parental panel = biallelic SNPs genotyped in nearly all parents; informative sites = panel sites where the mother and father are homozygous for different alleles (REF/ALT must agree between the trio VCF and the imputed infant VCF); at each informative site where the infant is a phased heterozygote, the left haplotype votes maternal if it carries the mother’s allele, otherwise paternal. Majority wins; ties are undefined. Output HAP_ORIGIN has one row per chromosome and columns <ID>_L, <ID>_R; HAP_ORIGIN.votes.tsv records the vote counts. 1.5.7 Stage 06 - maternal / paternal count matrices ornaments_summarizeToGene.R --level gene|transcript, per sample: within-gene transcript usage weights w_t = TPM_t / sum TPM (equal weights if all transcripts of a gene have TPM 0); Ornaments haplotype counts (L, R) to maternal / paternal using HAP_ORIGIN for that chromosome (undefined haplotypes contribute 0); transcript level: feature = transcript:tx_pos; gene level: transcript positions are mapped back to genomic SNPs and feature = gene:chr:pos, count = sum over the gene’s transcripts carrying that SNP of w_t x count_t. Columns are <sample>_maternal, <sample>_paternal; absent features are 0. 1.5.8 Stage 07 - baseline parent-of-origin effects model_inputs.R: joins covariates and PFAS tables; modelled samples are those present in the counts and metadata, not excluded, with non-missing sex and ancestry. Codes each condition in POE_CONDITIONS (continuous or binary), computes median-of-ratios size factors over maternal + paternal counts, filters features (>= 3 SNPs, >= 15 samples, >= 50 total counts), and splits features into N_BATCHES_GENE + N_BATCHES_TX balanced batches of long tables. fit_baseline.R (array): per feature, glmmTMB negative binomial (nbinom2) count ~ allele + sex + ancestry + (1|SNPpos) + (1|sample_id) + offset(log SF) beta = log(paternal / maternal) expression ratio. Counts are rounded. combine_baseline.R: gathers all batches (fails if any is missing) and applies Benjamini-Hochberg within each level. baseline_report.R: significance tier = BH q < 0.10 and the 95% CI of beta entirely outside +/- log(1.5) (60:40 allelic ratio). Volcano, forest, p-value, QQ and observed-vs-predicted calibration plots; transcript-gene overlap; Fisher test for enrichment of known imprinted genes among POE genes. within_sample.R: per sample, exact binomial test of maternal vs paternal counts per SNP, ACAT-combined per feature (count weights), BH within sample. A feature is biased in a sample if q < 0.05 and maternal ratio < 0.1 or > 0.9. 1.5.9 Stage 08 - PFAS / GDM x parent-of-origin interaction fit_interaction.R (array, same batches as stage 07): per feature and condition X (samples with missing X dropped), count ~ allele * X + ancestry + sex + (1|SNPpos) + (1|sample_id) + offset(log SF) beta_int = change in the POE log-ratio per unit of X. For continuous X the POE is also reported at X = 0, at +1 SD, at the mean and mean + 1 SD of the modelled samples, and along a dose grid of -8..8 (delta-method 95% CIs). Binary X (GDM) reports the POE in each group. Each feature uses a seed derived from its ID, so results do not depend on batch layout. combine_interaction.R: BH within each level x condition. interaction_report.R: tiers via classify_poe_nbmm_diff; hits = q_int < 0.10 and |beta_int| > log(1.5). Volcano, p-value, QQ and forest plots per condition, hit summaries for every condition, overlap with imprinted genes, gene-transcript overlap, bar charts of strict hits per PFAS (maternal and cord). dose_response.R: for conditions in DOSE_RESPONSE_CONDITIONS, predicted maternal allelic ratio across the exposure range for each hit, cohort-centred (annotated with the whole-cohort mean / SD) and centred on the modelled samples. 1.5.10 Stage 09 - power power_analysis.R: power of the baseline POE test versus sample size, simulated from the observed baseline standard errors (scaled by sqrt(n0/N)), for a fraction pi1 in {0.5%, 1%, 2%} of features carrying a true effect of ratio 1.5-1.8, discoveries at BH q < 0.10 and |beta| >= log(1.5), 1000 studies per scenario. Runs for both levels. power_plot.R: power to detect allelic imbalance and its change with exposure by allele-specific read depth, from the Bayesian ASE simulation summary shipped in 09_power/. 1.5.11 Stage 10 - mediation simulation (independent) PFAS_imprinting_sim.R simulates null studies (n = 100, 1000 isoforms) of the planned PFAS -> imprinted isoform -> outcome (SRS) mediation analysis and compares the type-I error of SEM (lavaan, bootstrap), CoCA, PGC and an adjusted linear model. Array element r uses seed r. aggregate_PFAS_sim_results.R summarises type-I error across runs; DAG.R draws the analysis DAG. 1.6 6. Resources and tuning config/resources.sh sets wall time, cores and memory per step (RES_<step>) and array concurrency (ARR_<step>). Job scripts read the cores actually granted (LSB_DJOB_NUMPROC), so changing -n is the only edit needed to scale a step. To size Ornaments (or any array step): ./run_pipeline.sh --submit 04_ornaments --pilot 2 tools/lsf_usage_report.sh 04_ornaments # peak memory and run time per job # edit RES_04_ornaments, then submit the rest: ./run_pipeline.sh --submit 04_ornaments Model batch counts (N_BATCHES_GENE, N_BATCHES_TX) control how many array elements stages 07-08 use; changing them requires rerunning 07_inputs. 1.9 9. Design notes and caveats PFAS scale is whatever the input CSVs contain (section 3.3). The dose grid of the cohort-centred dose-response plot is in those units; the subset-centred plot is in SDs of the modelled samples. Effect-size threshold. Baseline and interaction hits use log(1.5) (a 60:40 allelic ratio). Stricter thresholds such as log(2.33) (70:30) or log(2.5) can be applied to the saved results with classify_poe_nbmm(). Covariates. Models adjust for sex and ancestry. Gestational age is read into the metadata but is not in the model formulas. Size factors are computed once on all modelled samples and reused for every condition. Haplotype origin is assigned per chromosome. Infants homozygous at an informative site and sites whose alleles differ between the trio and imputed VCFs do not vote; haplotypes with tied votes are undefined and contribute no counts. Ancestry for infants without reported ethnicity comes from a 3-NN classifier on two PCs; check ancestry_assignments.tsv and the PCA figure. Phasing uses SHAPEIT5 phase_common with the trio pedigree. Check that the pedigree IDs match the VCF sample IDs (ID_MODE, section 5, stage 01). Within-sample tests are descriptive; cohort-level inference comes from the NB-GLMMs. Reports. The HTML reports in docs/reports/ are rendered documents; their Rmd sources in reports/ reference figure files that are not part of this repository (see reports/README.md). 1.10 10. 2 Genotyping methods 2.1 DNA and arrays Maternal DNA was extracted from blood collected at mid-gestation, infant DNA from umbilical cord tissue or blood, and paternal DNA from buccal swabs. DNA extraction for mothers and infants was as described previously [1-3]. Isohelix DNA buccal swabs stored at -80 C were equilibrated to room temperature for 1 h; 1 mL of ATL lysis buffer (Qiagen) was added and incubated at room temperature for 30 min, then 100 uL of proteinase K (Qiagen) was added and incubated at 60 C with shaking for 30-60 min. DNA was extracted from the lysates with QIAsymphony DNA kits according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Paternal buccal-swab DNA (n = 732), maternal buffy-coat DNA collected at 26-28 weeks of gestation (n = 1079) and umbilical-cord DNA from the children (n = 1073) were genotyped on the Illumina OmniExpressExome-8 v1.2 array (~1 million SNPs) [3]. Hybridisation and scanning were performed by Expression Analysis, Inc. (Morrisville, North Carolina). Data were processed with the GenomeStudio Genotyping Module (Illumina): genotypes were called by GenCall (GenTrain clustering, Bayesian calling), and genotypes with a GenCall score < 0.15 were set to missing. 2.2 Array-level QC (before this pipeline) Principal components analysis confirmed self-reported ethnicity. Samples with call rate < 97%, cryptic relatedness, or sex / ethnicity discrepancies were excluded. Alleles are reported on hg19. SNP QC was done separately in the Chinese, Malay and Indian subgroups: a SNP was dropped if call rate < 0.95, MAF < 0.05 or Hardy-Weinberg P < 1e-6. The resulting PLINK files (one each for infants, mothers and fathers) and the array manifest are the genotype inputs of stage 01. 2.3 Processing in this pipeline Step What it does 01_genotype_prep/prep_ped.R trio pedigree from the three .fam files 01_genotype_prep/plink2vcf.lsf merge, TOP strand -> hg19 forward strand (bcftools +fixref), REF check 01_genotype_prep/liftover.lsf hg19 -> GRCh38, biallelic SNPs with GRCh38-matching REF 01_genotype_prep/check_mendel.lsf Mendelian error rates 02_ancestry_phasing/infer_ancestry.R PCA + 3-NN ancestry for infants without reported ethnicity 02_ancestry_phasing/split_by_ancestry.lsf per-group filters: missingness <= 0.05, MAF >= 0.05, HWE p >= 1e-6 02_ancestry_phasing/phase.lsf SHAPEIT5 pedigree-aware phasing per group and chromosome 03_imputation_SEAD/ SEAD imputation of phased infants; biallelic, MAF > 0.01, Rsq >= 0.3 See WORKFLOW.md for details. 2.4 References Chen L, Pan H, Tuan TA, et al. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) Val66Met polymorphism influences the association of the methylome with maternal anxiety and neonatal brain volumes.
